bull.b: Debt elimination lowers fixed financing costs and reduces exposure to bitcoin-collateral volatility. The added unrestricted capital improves liquidity and gives Fold more flexibility to fund products while pursuing operational stabilization.

The regulated-bank relationship and proprietary ledger can broaden Fold beyond bitcoin transactions into deposits, banking services, and asset-based revenue. This infrastructure may support a more diversified and recurring business model over time.

Early customer usage and reported profitable per-swipe economics indicate potential product-market fit. A large applicant pipeline provides a foundation for scaling card revenue and customer engagement if financing capacity expands.

bear.b: Large losses and sustained negative operating and free cash flow show that the business is not yet self-funding. Continued investment in products may require external capital, leaving execution dependent on improving margins and cash conversion.

Declining revenue and worsening quarterly adjusted EBITDA undermine confidence in near-term operating leverage. High gross margin has not translated into positive EBIT or EBITDA, so the new products must scale materially to change the earnings profile.

Self-financing receivables limits how quickly Fold can expand card issuance and credit access. Until strategic funding partners are secured, growth may consume internal liquidity and constrain the commercial benefit of strong demand indicators.
